name: Andronicus
overview: Andronicus is a male believer mentioned in the New Testament as a kinsman and fellow prisoner of the Apostle Paul. His association with Paul highlights his close connection to the early Christian mission during a time of persecution. No additional tribal or familial details are recorded in Scripture.
namesAndTitles: The name Andronicus appears as a proper name in Romans 16:7, with no specific meaning or divine origin indicated in the biblical text. It is simply presented as his personal name without additional titles or meanings.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Andronicus beyond his identification as a kinsman to Paul. No other relatives or relationships are mentioned in the biblical account.
scriptureSignificance: Andronicus is significant for his close association with Paul, being both a relative and a fellow prisoner, which suggests his faithful commitment to Christ even under hardship. His mention by Paul in Romans 16:7 affirms his respected status among the early Christians and his partnership in the gospel ministry. This brief but notable reference underscores the unity and perseverance of believers in the face of persecution.
